review.scope: Readiness discussion after operator charter ratification: optional legacy preview, fail closed on conflicting preview, stable legacy dedup and context-bound ratified discussion identities. Source-only review, no execution. Existing patient and standing activation gates remain held.
findings: BLOCKER (verified in supplied source): the conflicting-preview refusal exists only in orchestrator/readiness_discussion.py. orchestrator/campaign_pipeline.py execute() remains reachable with a proposal preview (including via its __main__ --proposal-context CLI for adoption/readiness/discuss/brief/curate modes) while a ratified selection is present: grounding() merges selected_prediction_context() into the context, then the 'if proposal:' block runs context.update(proposal_context(...)), whose context-disposition.json (EXPLICIT_PROPOSAL_PREVIEW_ONLY, ratified false, next_gate operator_charter_ratification) overwrites the ratified disposition (OPERATOR_SELECTED_CONDITIONAL_BASELINE, ratified true, launch_authorized false). Pre-ratification callers habitually passed exactly this preview path, so the same invocation now yields a bound context misrepresenting the operator's recorded ratification as pending, and a different proposal directory merges two competing charter contexts under colliding keys. No authority escalation (the overwrite downgrades authority), but the change's stated fail-closed invariant is broken on a supported entry point. Smallest correction: raise in execute()/grounding() when selected_prediction_context() is nonempty and proposal is not None, mirroring RATIFIED_CONTEXT_REFUSES_PROPOSAL_PREVIEW.

SUGGESTION: discuss() calls public_export.text(json.dumps(packet)) before the ratified/preview conflict check, the SELECTED_OR_PREVIEW_CONTEXT_REQUIRED check and the dedup lookup, so refused and duplicate invocations still re-export the packet externally on every call. Per-event METADATA_ONLY scope is checked first, so this is repeated export rather than a privacy leak; move the export after validation and the duplicate short-circuit or make it idempotent per identity.

SUGGESTION: the legacy identity is events-only (intentional for dedup stability), so a second legacy call with a different --proposal preview silently returns the first discussion as duplicate, and neither the readiness_discussions row nor the duplicate return records which preview the executed discussion actually used. Record the proposal path/receipt hash in the row or output, or fail closed when a differing preview targets an already-discussed event set.

SUGGESTION: the ratified identity hashes the entire operating context including task_state with the live decision_inbox and full document contents, so inbox churn or any unrelated document edit mints a new discussion identity and a new model call for an unchanged event set and unchanged ratified selection, weakening the one-discussion-per-completion-set bound. Bind version, events and the selected_scientific_context hashes (plus canonical document sha256s) instead of the raw operating packet.

SUGGESTION (partly inferred; immutable() source not supplied): the discussion-context artifact is written via immutable() before the CLAIMED row INSERT; a crash in that window leaves an orphan artifact and a rerun of the identical identity will presumably fail on the existing immutable file with no row explaining why. Fail-closed, but add an explicit reconcile path or write the artifact after the insert.

Verified sound (source-only, tests read not run): selected_prediction_context fails closed with exact status match, scope asserting charter_ratified/conditional_external_seed_adoption exactly true and patient_launch/new_backend_patient_transfer/reserved_cohort_access exactly false, complete hash binding of all proposal artifacts to the decision, and launch_authorized false in the disposition; build() preserves historical charter bytes under a relabeled disposition and drops the fixed-path preview when a selection exists; discuss() recovery is fail-closed via CLAIMED_RECONCILE_IF_INTERRUPTED/BLOCKED_RECONCILE_NO_AUTOMATIC_RETRY with no automatic retry; the request text restates patient-launch, 047-landing and unattended-activation gates and forbids re-requesting a recorded ratification; nothing in the change touches patient-data paths or held activation gates.
